column1: # Hand-curated transfer history + reported fees.
# This file serves two purposes:
#   1. Reported fee data feeds the v2 EUR regression as the highest-
#      authority training signal (source weight 3.0
#   2. The metadata columns (transfer_type
#      provide context for scouting and modelling
#      for the regression itself.
# Schema:
#   playerId         Wyscout integer ID. Look up via Player Profile page.
#   player_name      Human-readable (free text — for sanity
#   from_team        Selling/releasing club.
#   to_team          Buying/receiving club.
#   transfer_type    One of:
#                      permanent          — outright transfer
#                      loan               — temporary
#                      loan_with_option   — loan with buy option (record option in notes)
#                      buy_option         — option from a previous loan was exercised
#                      free               — free transfer (fee_eur should be 0 or blank)
#                      end_of_contract    — contract ran out
#                      mutual_termination — contract dissolved early
#                      release_clause     — release clause triggered
#                      pre_contract       — pre-contract signed (Bosman-style)
#                      offer              — bid received but NOT completed.
#                                           fee_eur = offer amount; feeds the
#                                           EUR model as market-price evidence
#                                           (loader ignores transfer_type
#                                           it trains like a paid fee). Record
#                                           outcome (rejected/pending) in notes.
#   fee_eur          Base transfer fee in EUR. Blank/0 = free/loan-without-fee.
#   add_ons_eur      Performance-based add-ons in EUR (if reported).
#   sell_on_pct      Percentage of next sale owed back to selling club (0-100).
#   as_of_date       Date of transfer (YYYY-MM-DD).
#   season_id        Wyscout seasonId the transfer landed in.
#   contract_until   Length of new contract at receiving club (YYYY-MM-DD).
#   loan_until       For loans only: when the loan ends (YYYY-MM-DD).
#   source_url       Press article / TM URL where fee was reported.
#   notes            Free text — agent
#                    rejected bids
# Tips for filling rows:
#   - Lines starting with `#` are ignored by load_valuations.py.
#   - Leave `fee_eur` blank for loans-without-fee or free transfers; they
#     still get included in the ledger but are filtered from the EUR-model
#     training data automatically.
#   - You don't have to fill every column for every row — minimum is
#     playerId
# SYNTHETIC TRANSFERS:
# To expand the training set with "transfers that could have happened" you can
# add rows with synthetic_flag=1. They feed the EUR regression exactly like
# real reported fees do (same source='reported_fee'
# to anchor your domain knowledge — "a 28yo perf-75 CB in Liga 3 would sell for
# ~€150k" — and to fill position/age gaps the 8 real transfers don't cover.
# For synthetic rows:
#   - playerId must point to a real Wyscout player so we can join GPA perf
#   - as_of_date should be a date during the season you want to "anchor"
#     (so the player's perf for THAT season is what we'd be training against)
#   - season_id should match the as_of_date's football year
#   - fee_eur is your best estimate of what the player would sell for
#   - synthetic_flag=1 marks it as hypothetical (audit-only — model treats
#     synthetic and real fees identically)
